newsitem.title: JAPAN: Greenspan says sceptical on currency ranges.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan says sceptical on currency ranges.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan told a news conference in Tokyo on Tuesday that he was sceptical about the concept of currency ranges.
"Until I see some evidence...that such types of ranges really do work, I would be sceptical," he said.
Referring to opinions about currency ranges held by financial analysts such as Fred Bergsten, he added:
"I'm less inclined to believe you can implement these kinds of ranges.
"The type of system we have probably is about as good as we are going to get for the time being."
Greenspan also said that he felt the "Big Bang" financial reform plan announced by Japan last week would contribute to the wider use of the yen as an international currency.
"I don't see how it can fail," he said, adding that "one of the basic problems in not investing in yen-based securities is the underlying structure".

Greenspan said he had no real views on the issue of whether it was better for central banks or finance ministries to have control over currency market intervention, adding that in the United States there was "de facto collaboration" between the central bank and the Treasury.
Concerning past experience of joint currency intervention with Japan, he said: "We have found the system works pretty seamlessly and have been quite pleased."
Japan is currently working on reform of the law governing the Bank of Japan with the aim of boosting the central bank's independence.
Greenspan arrived in Japan on Sunday for meetings with financial and monetary authorities. He was scheduled to leave later on Tuesday.
